LINQ over files

ParquetNeo.Linq queries a file, or all the files of a directory (and the folders below it), with LINQ. It is not trim or Native AOT safe: it reads expression trees and builds types at run time.

using ParquetNeo.Linq;

var people = ParquetDataset.Open<Person>("people/");
var names = people.Where(p => p.Born >= new DateOnly(1900, 1, 1) && p.Name != null)
                  .OrderBy(p => p.Born)
                  .Select(p => new { p.Name, p.Born })
                  .Take(100)
                  .ToList();

ParquetDataset<T> is an IQueryable<T>. Every operator of LINQ to objects works on the rows that are read, and what is added is what lets it read less:

  • Files, row groups and pages are skipped. The Wheres at the start of the query are turned into a ParquetFilter (see Skipping what is not needed): comparisons with constants and captured values, null tests, boolean properties, Contains on a list, nested properties, &&, || and !. The whole predicate is still applied to the rows that are read, so the result is exact.
  • Only the columns a query uses are read, when it ends in a Select after only Wheres, ordering and paging.
  • Count(), LongCount() and Any() are answered from the footers of the files when they can be.
  • Files are read in parallel, so without an OrderBy the rows come in no particular order.
var plan = people.Where(p => p.Id > 5000).Explain();   // which files and row groups are skipped, which columns are read
int count = people.Count();                            // from the footers: no data is read
await foreach (var row in people.Where(p => p.Id > 5000).AsAsyncEnumerable()) { }

AsAsyncEnumerable, ToListAsync, ToArrayAsync, FirstAsync, FirstOrDefaultAsync, CountAsync and AnyAsync run the query on another thread and do not block the caller.

Datasets are local files for now.
